record.original_question: Fix integers s and q with gcd(s,q) = 1, and a digit set D = {d_0, ..., d_k} with 0 = d_0 < d_1 < ... < d_k < s, 1 <= k <= s - 2, and gcd(d_0, ..., d_k) = 1. Let K_s^D(N) be the set of positive integers x < N whose base-s digits all lie in D. Is it true that for some sufficiently large sigma > 0, whenever N >= q^sigma, every residue class lambda modulo q is represented by some x in K_s^D(N)?

evidence.quote: For positive integers s, k we consider sets D = {d0 , ..., dk }, 0 = d0 < d1 < ... < dk < s, 1 ⩽ k ⩽ s − 2, (d1 , ..., dk ) = 1, KsD (N) = {x ∈ Z+ : x < N, x = Σ δj sj , δj ∈ D}.
Suppose that (s, q) = (d0 , ..., dk ) = 1, k ⩾ 2. Is it true that for some large σ > 0 for N ⩾ qσ for any λ (mod q) there exists x ∈ KsD (N) such that x ≡ λ (mod q) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $s \geq 3$ and $q \geq 2$ be integers with $\gcd(s,q)=1$. Let $D = \{d_0, d_1, \ldots, d_k\}$ be a set of base-$s$ digits with $0 = d_0 < d_1 < \cdots < d_k < s$, where $2 \leq k \leq s-2$ and $\gcd(d_1, \ldots, d_k) = 1$. For a positive real number $N$, define
$$K_s^D(N) = \Big\{\, x \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0} : x < N, \ x = \sum_{j \geq 0} \delta_j s^j \text{ with } \delta_j \in D \text{ for all } j \,\Big\}.$$
That is, $K_s^D(N)$ consists of the positive integers below $N$ all of whose base-$s$ digits lie in $D$.

Prove or disprove: there exists a constant $\sigma > 0$ (allowed to depend on $s$ and $D$) such that for every $N \geq q^{\sigma}$ and every residue class $\lambda \pmod{q}$, there exists $x \in K_s^D(N)$ with $x \equiv \lambda \pmod{q}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Konyagin and collaborators have established average distribution and character-sum bounds for integers with missing digits in residue classes (e.g., Konyagin, Period. Math. Hungar. 2001; Banks–Conflitti–Shparlinski 2007). However, the surjectivity question — that every residue class mod $q$ is represented by a missing-digits integer below $q^{\sigma}$ for some fixed $\sigma$ — does not appear to be settled in the literature found. Status appears open.

status_evidence.title: Arithmetic properties of integers with missing digits: distribution in residue classes
status_evidence.snippet: Numbers with missing digits are in average well-distributed in residue classes mod m where averaging is taken over m.
status_evidence.claim: Only average (over moduli) distribution is established, not the per-modulus surjectivity sought in the problem.

status_evidence.title: On the multiplicative properties modulo m of numbers with missing digits
status_evidence.snippet: Upper bounds for character sums modulo a composite number over sets of numbers with missing digits, with applications to congruences x_1 ... x_t ≡ λ (mod m).
status_evidence.claim: Related work obtains character-sum bounds and multiplicative congruence solvability, but does not resolve the additive single-variable surjectivity conjecture.
